results.title: LOKI: An LLM Accelerator with Optimized KV Cache and In-Memory Computing Cores
results.venue: International Symposium on Circuits and Systems
results.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are scaling rapidly, both in model size and context length, leading to rapidly increasing compute and memory demands during inference. The quadratic growth of attention mechanisms with sequence length imposes heavy key-value (KV) cache storage and bandwidth requirements, which dominate inference costs. Efficient KV cache management has thus become crucial for scalable and energy-efficient LLM deployment on hardware. This paper presents LOKI—a network-on-chip (NoC)-based accelerator architecture designed to address these challenges using system-level KV cache distribution and importance-driven KV cache pruning. Each processing element (PE) integrates an in-memory computing (IMC) core for weight-stationary (WS) matrix operations, digital attention blocks for pruned attention computation, and scratchpad memories for distributed KV cache storage. A dual-mode dataflow adapts to the distinct computational needs of the prefill and decode phases. Experimental results show that LOKI achieves 155.8× higher energy efficiency and 1.87× greater throughput compared to NVIDIA A100 GPU.

results.title: MoEsaic: Shared Mixture of Experts
results.abstract: Mixture of Expert (MoE) models consist of several experts, each specializing in a specific task. During inference, a subset of the experts is invoked based on their relevance to the request. MoE's modular architecture lets users compose their model from popular off-the-shelf experts. This leads to multiple MoE deployments with identical experts. The duplication of experts across model instances results in excessive GPU memory consumption and increased model serving cost. Moreover, since all experts are not invoked for each request, individual experts rarely receive enough requests to exploit the GPUs' computational capabilities, resulting in low GPU utilization. To address these problems, we propose Shared Mixture of Experts in MoEsaic. MoEsaic automatically identifies and deduplicates identical experts across model instances, thus reducing their memory footprint. Moreover, it batches the requests directed toward the identical experts belonging to different clients, which also improves the processing efficiency. We show that for Mixtral-8x7B model, when compared to deploying dedicated MoE instances, MoEsaic can serve 7X more model instances with little impact on inference performance.
